Question kind: abnormal_behavior_prediction

Question:
Use `faker_qa/credit_card_provider_empty_types_indexerror_uncaught/files/testcase.py`, class `TestCreditCardProviderEmptyTypesIndexErrorUncaughtQA`, method `test_credit_card_provider_empty_types_indexerror_uncaught_case`. After `seed_instance(2357)`, the test calls `credit_card_number` (Luhn construction via `_generate_number`), `credit_card_expire` (date range parsing), and `credit_card_security_code` (numeric pattern from the selected card type). It then resolves `faker.providers.credit_card` via `Generator.provider` and replaces `credit_card_types` with an empty `OrderedDict`, removing every `CardType` entry. The final `fake.credit_card_provider()` enters `faker/providers/credit_card/__init__.py::Provider.credit_card_provider` with `card_type is None`, so execution reaches `self.random_element(self.credit_card_types.keys())` (lines 114–115) over an empty key set. What exact exception type and exception message are thrown as an uncaught exception from that `credit_card_provider` invocation (i.e., the exception that propagates out of the credit_card provider and is caught by the test harness)?

{"exception_message":"str","exception_type":"str"}
